content:
Plan for Phase 67, first of the cockpit arc (Phases 67–74 added to docs/roadmap.md at 7bc0986 after a design discussion with the arbiter: the cockpit replaces the three iTerm2 tabs; the watcher sits behind a turn bar and expands to its history).

Plan: docs/phases/watcher-event-log-and-heartbeat.md. Engine + CLI + two read endpoints, no UI.
- New tagteam/watchlog.py: bounded .tagteam/watcher-events.jsonl (512 KB + one .1, best-effort O_APPEND writes, guarded reads via safe_read) and an atomic, throttled .tagteam/watcher-beat.json carrying every_s.
- watcher._log(msg, kind='info', **ctx) keeps printing as today and feeds a sink installed only inside _watch_locked(); ~25 dispatch-relevant call sites get a kind from a closed vocabulary. No control flow moves; gate/panel/briefer/engine lines arrive as info through the log=_log they already receive.
- tagteam watch status / watch log [-n N] [--json], both allowed under TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY; every existing watch invocation unchanged.
- GET /api/watcher/events; now.watcher gains beat_age_s and last_event.

Please rule on the section 'Decision for the reviewer and arbiter': watcher.json is opt-in under a 3.0-arc rule (a bare tagteam watch writes nothing new into the project). I recommend every watcher writes the log and beat (option A) because the iTerm2 workflow runs without --pidfile and .tagteam/ is already tagteam's runtime dir; option B gates it like the pidfile. Also worth your eye: a stale beat is a problem only when no turn is in flight (headless blocks the loop), and staleness is judged against every_s because the poll loop (10 s) and event loop (30 s) differ.

Verified while planning: roadmap check ok (75 phases, 31 edges); gate check --skip-tests plan-doc ok. Nothing implemented.

Reviewed plan at 7bc0986 and the watcher, watcher_events, and cockpit_api integration points. Option A is approved as the scoped product choice: record for every watcher when .tagteam already exists, without changing the pidfile opt-in. Update the old no-new-project-files comments to describe this exception. No arbiter decision is needed on A versus B.

Please revise three implementation requirements before proceeding:

1. Guard writes, not just reads. append currently specifies O_APPEND and swallowing OSError, which can still block indefinitely opening a FIFO and can append through a symlink. Specify nonblocking/no-follow open with regular-file verification and checked parent paths, plus safe rotation and heartbeat temp-file handling. Keep failures best-effort for both event and beat writes. Add deterministic writer FIFO/symlink tests proving dispatch proceeds and no linked target is modified. Replace the absolute promise that synchronous filesystem I/O can never slow dispatch with the actual bounded/best-effort guarantee (or explicitly design asynchronous logging if the absolute guarantee is intended).

2. Serialize the new writer state within the process. The one-watcher lock does not imply one calling thread: watcher_events.watch_with_events invokes on_change from the watchdog observer and from the main startup/heartbeat loop. These can concurrently log and update the beat. Plan a per-sink lock around rotation + append and heartbeat throttle + replacement, with a concurrent-caller regression. Do not expand this into a processor/control-flow redesign; this request concerns the new logging state. O_APPEND alone does not serialize rotation.

3. Complete the heartbeat reader/API contract. now.watcher exposes only beat_age_s, yet the plan explicitly requires consumers to judge staleness using every_s (variable --interval versus event mode). Expose the cadence or an equivalent derived stale fact. Define how a beat is associated with the current watcher so an old beat surviving an unclean exit is not presented as a new process's last look; include process identity/session information as needed. Also define a valid in-flight exemption (a live matching cycle runner, not just any leftover or conversational in-flight marker). Cover previous-watcher beats, missing/malformed beats, custom poll intervals, and live versus stale/unrelated in-flight markers. Beat cleanup must run for option-A watchers even when keep_pidfile is false.

No implementation or full-suite run was needed for this plan review. Existing scope exclusions and no-UI boundary are appropriate.

Plan revised at dcf4f2e (docs/phases/watcher-event-log-and-heartbeat.md). Option A recorded as decided in review; the two 3.0-arc 'writes nothing new' comments (pidfile block, WatcherLock) are now in scope to update with the exception; pidfile opt-in unchanged; .tagteam/ is never created for this.

1. Guarded writes. One private _open_regular(): parent chain via safe_read._dir_chain (symlinked/non-dir parent refuses); leaf opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC and fstat-verified S_ISREG before any byte. Rotation is os.replace (renames the entry, never follows a link at either name), size taken from the verified fd. Beat temp file is O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW with one unlink-and-retry. Event and beat writes are both best-effort. The absolute 'can never slow a dispatch' promise is replaced by the real guarantee: synchronous, bounded, non-blocking opens, no write through a link, failures swallowed; async logging explicitly not planned. Criterion 3 is now deterministic writer FIFO/symlink tests (event path, beat path, temp name, .tagteam itself) asserting dispatch proceeds and the link target is byte-identical.

2. Serialization. A Sink object owns one threading.Lock around (size check + rotation + append) and around (throttle + temp write + replace), because watch_with_events calls on_change from the observer thread and the main loop. Scoped to the new logging state only; no processor change. Criterion 6a: concurrent callers across a rotation boundary, and two beats inside the throttle window.

3. Reader contract. The beat now carries pid, ident (procs.identity, as the pidfile does), started_at and every_s. One shared beat_view() used by the CLI and the API returns {state, age_s, every_s, stale_after_s}, state in none | previous | fresh | in-turn | stale: 'previous' when the beat's pid is dead, its ident differs, or it is not the running watcher's pid (unreadable identity does not alone demote, matching watcher_status); stale_after_s = 3 x every_s from the beat; 'in-turn' only for a cycle in-flight whose watcher_pid/ident match the beat and whose runner pid is alive — conversation/briefer, dead-runner and other-watcher in-flights do not exempt. now.watcher exposes 'beat' (that dict) instead of beat_age_s, so no consumer re-derives staleness. Beat cleanup is tied to the sink's finally, runs with keep_pidfile false, and only removes this pid's beat. Criterion 6b is the table test covering previous-watcher, missing/malformed, custom intervals and live vs stale/unrelated in-flight.

Verified: gate check --skip-tests not re-run (docs only); nothing implemented.

Approved revised plan at dcf4f2e. All three round-1 findings are addressed: guarded best-effort event/beat writes with deterministic failure coverage; per-Sink serialization for both event-loop calling threads; and a shared identity-aware beat_view contract exposing cadence and derived state, with cleanup independent of pidfile opt-in. Option A remains approved. The scope stays engine/CLI/read API, with no UI or processor redesign.

Implementation notes within the approved requirements:
- The effective heartbeat cadence must account for the 5-second throttle. For polling intervals below 5 seconds, do not declare a healthy watcher stale after 3 times the raw interval; use an effective cadence that includes throttling and cover a short-interval example.
- Preserve the leaf lstat refusal as well as parent checks and post-open fstat when adapting safe_read's discipline. getattr(O_NOFOLLOW, 0) alone does not refuse an existing leaf symlink on platforms without that flag. Describe the safeguards accurately rather than promising protection against every possible concurrent parent-directory replacement.

Reviewed the changed plan and existing safe_read/watcher integration; no implementation exists yet and no tests were run for this documentation-only plan review. No outstanding plan blockers or interjections.
